b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Said and Done
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the military governments, and he asks what the generals promised.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the military said and what they did.
cues: Say what the military said they wanted
Contrast it with what they did
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.target: Los militares decían que querían defender el orden. Sin embargo, no devolvieron el poder pronto.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.english: The military said they wanted to defend order. However, they did not give power back soon.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.canDo: I can contrast what the military said with what they did using *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Brazil, 1964
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading a book about Brazil and asks what happened to President Goulart.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.prompt: Tell Meg who was overthrown in 1964 and what happened to the Congress in 1968.
cues: Say who was overthrown and when
Say what happened to the Congress
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.target: El presidente Goulart fue derrocado en 1964. El Congreso fue cerrado durante varios meses.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.english: President Goulart was overthrown in 1964. Congress was closed for several months.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.canDo: I can say what was done using *ser* + past participle.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Chile, 1973
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just visited a museum exhibition about Chile.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what had happened in Chile before the coup.
cues: Say who had won the elections of 1970
Say what the country had gone through
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.target: Allende había ganado las elecciones de 1970, y el país ya había pasado por meses de crisis.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.english: Allende had won the elections of 1970, and the country had already gone through months of crisis.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.canDo: I can say what had already happened using *había* + participle.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Argentina, 1976
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a documentary on Argentina that you saw.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.prompt: Tell Meg what was done in 1976.
cues: Say what was done with the Congress
Say what was done with the political parties
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.target: En 1976 se cerró el Congreso y se suspendió la actividad de los partidos políticos.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.english: In 1976 Congress was closed and the activity of the political parties was suspended.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.canDo: I can say what was done using *se* without naming who did it.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of Military Rule
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you learned in a class about the end of the military governments.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.prompt: Tell Carlos why the Argentine military left power.
cues: Name the cause with a formal connector
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.target: A raíz de la derrota en la guerra de las Malvinas, los militares dejaron el poder en 1983.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.english: As a result of the defeat in the Malvinas war, the military left power in 1983.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.canDo: I can explain a cause using *debido a* or *a raíz de*.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Military Governments Review
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you what you remember from the class about military governments.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one thing about Chile and one about Argentina.
cues: Say who had won the elections of 1970 in Chile
Say who was the first president of the junta in Argentina
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.target: Allende había ganado las elecciones de 1970 en Chile. En Argentina, Videla fue el primer presidente de la junta.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.english: Allende had won the elections of 1970 in Chile. In Argentina, Videla was the first president of the junta.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.canDo: I can contrast what the military said with what they did.
